extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 that excludes a registered patent attorney from practice before the USPTO based on a state disbarment and related criminal convictions. The document sets out procedural service/notice rules, findings based on the respondent's failure to respond, and the required post-discipline notifications and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from practice under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, Respondent is hereby excluded from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs that Respondent is excluded from practice before the USPTO commencing on the date of the Final Order and shall remain excluded until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60. The Order also directs dissociation of Respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond to Notice and Order (40-day response period)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response is a key procedural fact; the Order treats an absence of response as supporting a finding that there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and proof of notice delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must be sent by certified mail and by non-certified first-class mail to the respondent's address(es); if initial attempts fail, alternative addresses may be used and certified mail receipts recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents certified mail receipt numbers and delivery dates (e.g., Notice and Order sent and delivered to specific addresses), indicating that proper service and proof of delivery are required for the proceeding to go forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline predicated on state disbarment (§ 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline under § 11.24 can be predicated upon a state disbarment; here, exclusion was for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disbarred by the Supreme Court of the State of Illinois.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the underlying misconduct supporting the state disbarment — January 2020 felony convictions for theft of sales tax in Florida and the Illinois Supreme Court's September 13, 2021 disbarment based on violations of Rule 8.4(b) — as the predicate for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis standard when respondent does not contest
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the OED may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and conclude that exclusion (reciprocal discipline) is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly states that in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is determined there is no genuine issue of material fact and exclusion is the appropriate discipline — effectively a default-finding standard when uncontested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement via petition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined respondent remains excluded until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order ties the duration of exclusion to the availability and granting of a reinstatement petition under the cited regulation; procedural and substantive requirements for such petitions are governed by § 11.60 (not detailed in this Order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and public access to disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides the FOIA Reading Room URL (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov) and instructs electronic publication to ensure public access to the disciplinary decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice contents and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion, the respondent's name and registration number, the predicate misconduct, the regulatory basis for discipline, and where disciplinary decisions are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a model 'Notice of Exclusion' specifying language to be used (e.g., respondent name, registration number, statement that respondent is excluded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), reference to state disbarment and Rule 8.4(b), statutory authority such as 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, and links to FOIA/OED).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires cross-jurisdictional notification so other disciplinary bodies and courts are informed of the USPTO action and its reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation of disciplined respondent to comply with duties in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order does not enumerate § 11.58 duties, it mandates compliance (e.g., duties commonly include notification and surrender obligations); the Order also couples this with directives such as dissociation from Customer Numbers and USPTO electronic accounts.
